newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rally led by technology stocks.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rally led by technology stocks.

text.p: Stock prices gained Wednesday on the back of a strong rebound in technology shares, but investors were assessing the chances for more interest rate hikes after the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time in more than two years on Tuesday.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 27.19 points at 6,903.36.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 275 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, was up 17.80 points at 1,265.86.

Investors were pondering the impact of Tuesday's quarter-point rise in interest rates by the central bank and the prospect that there could be further increases following stronger-than-expected February durable goods data.

The interest-rate hike will mean higher borrowing costs for consumer and corporate loans. Many commercial banks, including Chase Manhattan, the nation's largest bank, have boosted their lending rates in response to the Fed move.
The Fed described its rate rise -- the first since February 1995 -- as a "prudent step" designed to help prolong the economic expansion by keeping inflation low through the end of next year.
Investors are worried that the action could hurt corporate profits as consumers cut back on their spending.
Strong economic data on Wednesday fuelled speculation that further Fed tightening was to come.

The Commerce Department said durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent in February compared with an upwardly revised 4.1 percent increase in January. Economists in a Reuters survey had expected, on average, a 0.4-percent drop in February orders.
The strength in the economy "of course gets people worried about the next rate increase," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney.
In the bond market, the key 30-year Treasury bond was off a quarter point, raising its yield to 6.99 percent from 6.97 percent at Tuesday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
"We're starting to see some bargain-hunting come in," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers, of the strength in technology stocks.
"Some of these stocks have been pretty beaten down and people are starting to look at putting them in their portfolio" as the quarter nears a close, he said.

Nervous investors pulled out of financial stocks, seen vulnerable to rising interest rates. Chase Manhattan Corp. fell 1-1/8 to 100-5/8, BankAmerica Corp. slipped 2-1/4 to 109-3/4 and Morgan Stanley Group Inc. dropped 1 to 63-1/8.
The stocks of U.S. airlines gained after Lehman Brothers raised its first quarter earnings estimates on several carriers, citing what it viewed as an outlook for strong industry revenues.
United Airlines' parent UAL Corp. rose 1-1/4 to 66-1/4, American Airlines' parent AMR Corp. gained 1-1/4 to 85-1/2 and Delta Air Lines Inc. advanced 1-3/8 to 84-1/4.
